buildFixes: First LDT cloudbuild attempt failed at gcloud parse time: `_IMAGE_TAG: "cad-ingest-$BUILD_ID"` tried to embed the built-in $BUILD_ID substitution inside a user substitution's own default value, which Cloud Build cannot resolve at config-parse time. Fixed by keeping _IMAGE_TAG static and appending -$BUILD_ID directly in the steps/images list (the exact pattern hauska-factory's own cloudbuild.parcel-setback-cells.yaml uses). Same latent bug fixed pre-submit in the hauska-engine cloudbuild file.

Second LDT build attempt failed for a real, deeper reason: Dockerfile.cad-ingest-job's `RUN pnpm run typecheck:libs` ran a whole-monorepo `tsc --build` inside a from-scratch container with no incremental dist/ cache (.gcloudignore strips dist/**/dist from the build context), surfacing ~150 pre-existing strict-mode TypeScript errors across unrelated packages that have nothing to do with cad-ingest. Root-caused: lib/db's package.json exports raw .ts source directly, so tsx needs no dist/ build at runtime. Step removed; lib/cad-ingest's own package-level typecheck (which passes cleanly) is the correct scope.

finding3_deployedFromBranchNotMain.acknowledgement: Correct: both Cloud Run jobs were originally built and deployed from the feature-branch tips (legacy-design-tools b7042f58, hauska-engine b41446f9 -- itself already a merge of origin/main into the branch to catch up on PR #421, which landed on hauska-engine's main between this lane's branch creation and its merge attempt), not from a merged main commit.
finding3_deployedFromBranchNotMain.resolution: After merging both PRs, fetched origin/main fresh in both worktrees and diffed the merged main HEAD against the exact branch tip each deployed image was built from: `git diff origin/main <branch-tip> --stat` returned EMPTY for both repos (legacy-design-tools: 08de93dc vs b7042f58; hauska-engine: 99f9146f vs b41446f9). The squash-merge commits are new commit objects (different SHAs, flattened history) but their trees are byte-for-byte identical to what was already built and deployed -- no other change landed on either main between the last green CI run and the merge. Per the adversarial reviewer's own stated exception ('if you judge a rebuild-and-redeploy is unnecessary because the branch tip and post-merge main are guaranteed byte-identical..., say so explicitly and show the diff is empty'), a rebuild-and-redeploy was judged unnecessary and skipped, with the empty diffs shown above as the evidence, rather than silently skipped.
